distinctions.bnss-144-alongside-hma: BNSS s.144 (old CrPC s.125) is the standalone Magistrate-level maintenance remedy that needs NO HMA proceeding and applies while the marriage subsists. It must be cited ALONGSIDE HMA s.24/s.25 in every maintenance answer: BNSS s.144 for immediate/subsistence maintenance, HMA s.24 for interim maintenance inside a pending HMA case, HMA s.25 for permanent alimony at/after decree. Amounts across routes are set off against each other — never double-counted.
distinctions.hma-24-vs-hma-25: HMA s.24 = INTERIM maintenance pendente lite, only DURING a pending HMA proceeding, ends when the proceeding ends. HMA s.25 = PERMANENT alimony/maintenance, ordered AT or AFTER an HMA decree, and can be lump sum or periodical for life or a specified period. Citing s.24 as the permanent remedy (or citing only s.24 with no s.25 and no BNSS s.144) was the retest failure.

sections.title: Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings
sections.when_used: INTERIM maintenance DURING the pendency of any proceeding under the HMA (restitution of conjugal rights, judicial separation, divorce, nullity). Triggered when: (a) an HMA proceeding is pending or being filed, AND (b) either spouse has no independent income sufficient for her/his support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding. In the test case it applies ONLY if/when an HMA proceeding is filed — it does not apply standalone while no HMA case is pending. It is the interim, time-bound companion to HMA s.25, not a substitute for BNSS s.144 (which needs no HMA proceeding).

sections.title: Permanent alimony and maintenance
sections.when_used: PERMANENT alimony/maintenance ordered at the time of passing any decree under the HMA, or at any time subsequent thereto, on application by either spouse. Triggered when: (a) an HMA decree is being passed or has been passed (divorce, judicial separation, nullity), AND (b) the applicant spouse requires ongoing support after the marriage ends or is judicially separated. In the test case it does NOT apply yet — no divorce was asked for and no decree exists — but it must be named in the section set so the user understands the permanent route exists at decree stage, and so the s.24/s.25 distinction is explicit. It is the permanent counterpart of interim s.24.

sections.relief: Monetary reliefs: maintenance for the woman and the 8yo daughter, compensation for loss of earnings, medical expenses, school fees, loss/damage to property, and rent or alternate-accommodation costs where she has been kept out of the shared household. sections.title: Monetary reliefs
sections.when_used: Monetary reliefs for a woman who has suffered domestic violence (including economic abuse — here: 2 years of separation with NO maintenance paid, and eviction threats from the shared household). Triggered when: (a) the applicant is in a domestic relationship with the respondent, AND (b) domestic violence is alleged (economic abuse by withholding maintenance counts), AND (c) she has incurred or will incur expenses/losses: maintenance for herself and the 8yo daughter, loss of earnings, medical expenses, school fees, loss/damage to property, or rent/alternate accommodation costs. It is a fast, Magistrate-level route that can run alongside BNSS s.144.
